69.subject: Botany
69.text: In which of the following sets of organisms, does the external fertilization occur?
69.sol: When fertilization occurs outside the body of the organism, this type of gametic fusion is called external fertilization or external syngamy. The external medium such as water is required for this type of fertilization. Thus, in most aquatic organisms such as a majority of algae, fishes and amphibians, external fertilization occurs.

159.subject: Botany
159.sol: Golgi apparatus or Golgi complex is absent in prokaryotic cells (PPLO, bacteria and blue-green algae). It is present in all eukaryotic cells except sieve tubes of plants, sperms of bryophytes and pteridophytes and red blood corpuscles of mammals.

170.subject: Botany
170.text: What is common between chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts ?
options: Storage of starch, proteins and lipids
Ability to multiply by a fission-like process
170.sol: Chloroplast, chromoplast and leucoplast are all types of plastids which are classified on the basis of pigments they contain. Plastids are semiautonomous cell organelles bounded by two membranes and are found in only plant cells & some unicellular organisms (Euglena) of uncertain affinity. The common among all the three organelles are that they have ability to multiply by a fission like process because these organelles contain there own genetic material and protein synthesizing machinery, i.e., DNA, RNA and ribosom

376.subject: Botany
376.text: Assertion : When the ambient temperature is high and soil contains excess of water, the plants tend to lose water in the form of droplets from lenticels. Reason : Root pressure regulates the rate of loss of water form lenticels.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
376.sol: When the ambient temperature is high and soil contains excess water, the rate of transpiration is increased i.e., loss of water takes place from leaves through stomata. Lenticular transpiration is only 0.1 % of the total transpiration. It however continues day and night because lenticels have no mechanism of closure. The lenticels connect the atmospheric air with the cortical tissue of stem through intercellular spaces present amongst the complementary cells. Root pressure regulates the rate of loss of water from t

1202.subject: Physics
1202.text: Assertion: Transformers are used only in alternating current source not in direct current. Reason : Only a.c. can be stepped up or down by means of transformers.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1202.sol: Transformers which convert low voltages into higher ones are called step-up transformers, while those which convert high voltages into lower ones are called step-down transformers. This is possible only for a.c. source and not for d.c. source.

1206.subject: Physics
1206.text: Assertion : A capacitor of suitable capacitance can be used in an AC circuit in place of the choke coil. Reason : A capacitor blocks DC and allows AC only.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1206.sol: We can use a capacitor of suitable capacitance as a choke coil, because average power consumed in an ideal capacitor is zero. Therefore, like a choke coil, a condenser can reduce AC without power dissipation.

1823.subject: Physics
1823.text: The angular momentum of a moving body remains constant if

1823.sol: When the net external torque acting on a system is zero, the total angular momentum of the system remains constant. Therefore the angular momentum of a moving body remains constant if net external torque is not applied.

2192.subject: Zoology
2192.text: Assertion : Cephalisation is advantageous to an animal. Reason : Cephalisation improves the appearance of an animal.

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
2192.sol: Cephalisation is the concentration of nervous tissue and sense organs in or towards the anterior end forming a distinct head. It provides greater prominence and domination of the head over the rest of the body. However, it does not improve the appearance of the animal.

27851.text: Number of electron deficient molecules among the following PH 3 , B 2 H 6 , CCl 4 , NH 3 , LiH and BCl 3 is
27851.sol: A molecule is said to be electron deficient because there are not enough valence electrons to form the expected number of covalent bonds. For example, in B 2 H 6 , there are only 12 electrons, three from each boron atoms and six from hydrogen, while ethane possesses 14 such electrons. Also in BCl 3 , B has six electrons in its outermost orbit. So, the number of electron deficient molecules are 2.

56392.subject: Chemistry
56392.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
56392.text: Which block element from following are known as transition elements?
56392.sol: Transition elements (also known as transition metals) are elements that have partially filled d orbitals. IUPAC defines transition elements as an element having a d subshell that is partially filled with electrons, or an element that has the ability to form stable cations with an incompletely filled d orbital. In general, any element which corresponds to the d-block of the modern periodic table (which consists of groups 3-12) is considered to be a transition element.

57964.sol: The conjugate base of a Bronsted acid is formed by the removal of one proton ( H^+ ) from it. 71122.subject: Biology
71122.text: Person recovering from attack of measles developes __________ to measles, for the life time.
71122.sol: When a person is exposed to a live pathogen, develops the disease, and becomes immune as a result of the primary immune response, it is called naturally acquired active immunity. Since the exposure to the pathogen happens naturally and the body actively builds immunity, this is an example of natural acquired active immunity. Answer: natural acquired active immunity

78195.text: If x + 5 y = 4 and y + 5 x = -4 , then what is (x + y) equal to?
78195.sol: Given equations are x + 5 y = 4 and y + 5 x = -4 . Adding the two equations, we get: x + y + 5 x + 5 y = 0 (x + y) + 5 ( x + y xy ) = 0 (x + y) (1 + 5 xy ) = 0 This implies either x + y = 0 or 1 + 5 xy = 0 . Subtracting the second equation from the first, we get: x - y - 5 x + 5 y = 8 (x - y) + 5 ( x - y xy ) = 8 (x - y) (1 + 5 xy ) = 8 If 1 + 5 xy = 0 , the second factor becomes zero, which gives 0 = 8 , a contradiction. Thus, 1 + 5 xy 0 . Therefore, we must have x + y = 0 . Answer: 0

Nodules act as a site for nitrogen fixation
The enzyme nitrogenase catalyses the conversion of atmospheric N ₂ to NH ₃
80033.sol: Root nodules of leguminous plants harbour symbiotic bacteria, Rhizobium, which fixes atmospheric nitrogen and provides the plant with most or all of its nitrogen requirements. In return, they have access to a rich supply of carbohydrate. The fixation of atmospheric nitrogen ( N ₂ ) to ammonia ( NH ₃ ) occurs within the nodules, using the enzyme nitrogenase but this enzyme is very sensitive to oxygen and gets inhibited in oxygen rich environment. 80367.subject: Botany
80367.text: Plants which produce characteristic pneumatophores and show vivipary belong to:
80367.sol: This is a salt-tolerant plant group that grows in soil or waters of high salinity, coming into contact with saline water through its roots or by salt spray, such as in saline semi-deserts, mangrove swamps, marshes and sloughs and seashores. Halophytes growing in saline soils or near the delta of a river, show: Vivipary which is in-situ seed germination. The seeds, while remaining attached in the mother plant, germinate and then shaded off. Pneumatophores or the breathing roots are for gaseous exchange.

80459.sol: Development of a mature female gametophyte, i.e., embryo sac from a megaspore mother cell in an angiosperm plant requires 1 meiotic and 3 mitotic divisions.

80725.subject: Chemistry
80725.text: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is :
options: RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.
DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases.
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases.
80725.sol: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine as its four bases. RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and uracil as its four bases. Thus, the statement that DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases is correct. Answer: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.

working out the efficiency of oil driven automobile engines
measuring the activity of Saccharomyces cerevisae in producing curd on a commercial scale
working out the efficiency of RBCs about their capacity to carry oxygen
84790.sol: Decomposition of organic matter by microbes requires oxygen. 85128.subject: Zoology
85128.text: Geometric representation of age structure is a characteristic of:
85128.sol: Geometric representation of age structure is a characteristic of population. In most populations, individuals are of different ages. The proportion of individuals in each age group is called the age structure of the population.

85157.subject: Zoology
85157.text: Which of the following is important for speciation?
85157.sol: Speciation provides a framework for classifying biodiversity on Earth and is a central concept in evolutionary biology. Speciation refers to the origin of new species. It occurs by mutation, isolation and selection. For speciation to occur, two new populations must be formed from one original population, and they must evolve in such a way that it becomes impossible for individuals from the two new populations to interbreed.

85249.subject: Zoology
85249.text: Down's syndrome in humans is due to:
85249.sol: Down's syndrome a genetic disorder is due to the presence of an extra chromosome 21 also known as trisomy of chromosome 21 . Related Theory Down's syndrome is caused due to abnormal cell division. During mitotic and meiotic cell division the chromosome pair separate so that each cell gets the copy of each chromosome. In Down syndrome, the chromosomes are not able to separate, giving rise to cells with an unequal number of chromosomes (nondisjunction).

100254.text: Assertion : A body is momentarily at rest at the instant it reverses the direction. Reason : A body cannot have acceleration if its velocity is zero at a given instant of time.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true
100254.sol: Assertion is true: When a body reverses its direction of motion, its instantaneous velocity must be zero at that point (e.g., a ball thrown upwards momentarily stops at the peak before falling). For example, a ball thrown vertically upwards has zero velocity at its highest point, but its acceleration is still ' g ' (acceleration due to gravity).

107768.text: A covalent molecule with the general formula AX ₃ is observed to have a T-shaped geometry. What are the number of lone pairs of electrons on the central atom A and its hybridization state, respectively?
107768.sol: According to VSEPR theory, a molecule with the general formula AX ₃ having a T-shaped geometry must have 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs of electrons on the central atom. The total number of electron domains (steric number) is 3 + 2 = 5 . A steric number of 5 corresponds to sp^3d hybridization. The 5 electron pairs arrange themselves in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry, where the 2 lone pairs occupy equatorial positions to minimize repulsion, resulting in a T-shaped molecular geometry. Answer: 2, sp^3d

PHBV is a synthetic polymer with the ability to undergo bacterial degradation.
PHBV is a synthetic polymer primarily used in the construction industry.
120071.sol: PHBV is unique among synthetic polymers because it can undergo bacterial degradation in the environment, making it more environmentally friendly.

120181.subject: Chemistry
120181.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Mixture of styrene and methyl methacrylate can form ionic addition polymer
Low-density polythene is a poor conductor of electricity
120181.sol: Mixture of styrene and methyl methacrylate can form acopolymer. Other statements are correct.

120211.subject: Chemistry
120211.text: What is the term used to express the range of bacteria affected by an antibiotic?
120211.sol: The range of bacteria affected by an antibiotic is expressed as its spectrum of action.

120340.subject: Chemistry
120340.text: What is the chemical linkage present in arsphenamine (salvarsan) that resembles the linkage present in azodyes?
120340.sol: The -As = As- linkage present in arsphenamine resembles the -N = N - linkage present in azodyes.

120503.subject: Chemistry
120503.text: Which one of the following is not a surfactant?
options: CH ₃- ( CH ₂ )₁₄- CH ₂- NH ₂
CH ₃- ( CH ₂ )₁₆- CH ₂ OSO ₂⁻ Na ⁺
OHC - ( CH ₂ )₁₄- CH ₂- COO ⁻ Na ⁺
120503.sol: To act as surfactant, there should be both polar and non-polar ends in the molecules.

120550.subject: Chemistry
120550.text: What is the term for the cyclic five-membered ring formed in fructose?
120550.sol: The cyclic ring in fructose is a five-membered ring, known as furanose.

121975.subject: Botany
121975.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom. 2. They have true roots, stem or leaves. 3. The main plant body of the Bryophyte is diploid. 4. The plant body of bryophytes is less differentiated than that of algae 5. They do not possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures at all.
121975.sol: Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom. They lack true roots, stem or leaves. The main plant body of the Bryophyte is haploid.he plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. They lack true roots, stem or leaves. They may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures.

122177.subject: Botany
122177.sol: The cortex in coralloid roots of Cycas is divided into inner and outer regions by algal zone. The cells of this zone contain endophytic algal forms particularly Anabaena cycadeae and Nostoc punctiforme.

122929.subject: Botany
122929.text: Embryo Parts Function. A. Radicle 1. Develops into the shoot system B. Plumule 2. Develops into the root system C. Cotyledons 3. Contains food reserves D. Embryonal Axis 4. Connects the radicle and the plumule
122929.sol: The radicle develops into the root system; the plumule develops into the shoot system; cotyledons store food reserves; the embryonal axis connects the radicle and plumule.

123112.subject: Botany
123112.text: Best material for the study of mitosis in laboratory is:
123112.sol: Root tips are the best to study mitosis. It is characteristic of meristematic cells present at the tip of the roots that provide the most suitable and sufficient raw material to study the different mitosis stages. Anther shows meiotic divisions mostly. Related Theory Onion is a monocot plant and is the most commonly used root tip to study mitosis.

123115.subject: Botany
123115.sol: In mango, pericarp is differentiated into the exocarp, mesocarp and endocarp. Exocarp is form the outer covering of the fruit. Mesocarp is the edible part of the mango and is hard and stony (seed).

123306.subject: Botany
123306.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The vascular bundles in leaves are surrounded by bundle sheath cells. Reason: Bundle sheath cells in the leaves have thin walls for easy exchange of gases.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
123306.sol: The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells, not thin-walled ones.

123450.subject: Botany
123450.text: Match the tissues in List-I with the developmental processes responsible for their formation in List-II. List-I List-II (A) Tracheary elements (I) Dedifferentiation (B) Cork cambium (II) Redifferentiation (C) Secondary xylem (III) Differentiation Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123450.sol: (A) Tracheary elements are formed from primary meristems whose cells undergo maturation and lose their protoplasm to become dead at maturity. This process of maturation is called differentiation. (B) Cork cambium is a secondary meristem formed from living permanent cells (like cortical cells) that regain the capacity to divide. This regaining of division capacity is called dedifferentiation. (C) Secondary xylem is formed from the vascular cambium (a dedifferentiated tissue). The derivatives of vascular cambium lose

124104.subject: Botany
124104.text: Label a,b,c and d in the given figure.
options: a- Sugar b-Peripheral Protein c-Phospholipid bilayer d- Cholesterol
a- Cholesterol b-Peripheral Protein c-Phospholipid bilayer d- Sugar
a- Cholesterol b-Phospholipid bilayer c- Peripheral Protein d- Sugar

124153.subject: Botany
124153.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the mitochondria Reason: Golgi cisternae have concave cis and convex trans face
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
124153.sol: The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave trans or the maturing face.

124371.subject: Botany
124371.text: Match List I with List II regarding the cellular components of a typical eukaryotic plant cell: List I List II A. Chloroplast DNA I. Linear double-stranded DNA B. Nuclear DNA II. Circular double-stranded DNA C. Chloroplast Ribosomes III. 70S D. Cytoplasmic Ribosomes IV. 80S Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
124371.sol: Chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles that contain their own genetic material, which is a small, circular, double-stranded DNA molecule (A-II). The nuclear DNA of eukaryotes is linear and double-stranded, associated with histone proteins (B-I). The ribosomes found in the stroma of chloroplasts are smaller (70S) than the cytoplasmic ribosomes (80S) of eukaryotes (C-III, D-IV). Thus, the correct match is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV. Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

124558.subject: Botany
124558.text: Which auxin is derived from naphthalene?
124558.sol: Auxins like IAA and indole butyric acid (IBA) have been isolated from plants. NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2, 4-D (2, 4-dichlorophenoxyacetic) are synthetic auxins. The term ‘auxin’ is applied to the indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), and to other natural and synthetic compounds having certain growth regulating properties. They are generally produced by the growing apices of the stems and roots, from where they migrate to the regions of their action

124772.subject: Botany
124772.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators is responsible for breaking seed and bud dormancy, initiating germination in peanut seeds, and sprouting of potato tubers?
124772.sol: According to NCERT, Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, and promotes the sprouting of potato tubers. Abscisic acid (ABA) generally acts as a growth inhibitor and induces dormancy rather than breaking it. While Gibberellic acid is involved in breaking seed dormancy in certain cases, the specific examples of peanut seeds and potato tubers are directly attributed to ethylene. Cytokinins are primarily involved in cell division, overcoming apical dominance, and delaying senescen

124887.subject: Botany
124887.text: The rupture and fractionation do not usually occur in the water column in vessel/tracheids during the ascent of sap because of
124887.sol: The vertical conduction of water from root to aerial parts of plant is called ascent of sap. The water molecules remain joined to each other due to a force of attraction called cohesion force. This attraction is due to the presence of hydrogen bonds between them. The magnitude of this force is very high therefore, the continuous water column in the xylem cannot be broken easily due to the force of gravity or other obstructions offered by internal tissues in the upward movement of water. This adhesive property of wa

124908.subject: Botany
124908.text: Why must food be translocated to all non-green parts of green plants?
options: Because they are involved in photosynthesis
Because they need food for oxidation
124908.sol: Only green plants and cyanobacteria can prepare their own food; by the process of photosynthesis they trap light energy and convert it into chemical energy that is stored in the bonds of carbohydrates like glucose, sucrose and starch. We must remember that in green plants too, not all cells, tissues and organs photosynthesize; only cells containing chloroplasts, that are most often located in the superficial layers, carry out photosynthesis. Hence, even in green plants all other organs, tissues and cells that are n

125380.subject: Botany
125380.text: What are synthesized by the electron flow in non-cyclic photophosphorylation?
125380.sol: Living organisms have the capability of extracting energy from oxidisable substances and store this in the form of bond energy. Special substances like ATP, carry this energy in their chemical bonds. The process through which ATP is synthesised by cells (in mitochondria and chloroplasts) is named phosphorylation. Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light. When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then the PS I, a process called non-cycli

125567.subject: Botany
125567.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Synthesis of sugar is light reaction 2. Synthesis of ATP is dark reaction 3. Usually the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls of the mesophyll cells 4. Cyclic photophosphorylation also occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation
125567.sol: Usually the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls of the mesophyll cells, such that they get the optimum quantity of the incident light.

125640.subject: Botany
125640.text: In the stroma lamellae of chloroplasts, only Photosystem I is functional and cyclic photophosphorylation occurs. Under these conditions, how is the proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane primarily generated?
options: By the splitting of water molecules on the inner side of the membrane.
By the activity of NADP reductase enzyme located on the stroma side of the membrane.
By the transfer of electrons through an H-carrier, which transports protons from the stroma into the lumen.
A proton gradient is not established because Photosystem II is absent in stroma lamellae.
125640.sol: During cyclic photophosphorylation in the stroma lamellae, Photosystem II and the NADP reductase enzyme are absent. Therefore, there is no splitting of water (which normally adds protons to the lumen) and no reduction of NADP^+ (which normally removes protons from the stroma). However, ATP is still synthesised, which requires a proton gradient. This gradient is established solely by the cyclic flow of electrons through the electron transport chain. As electrons pass through the H-carrier (plastoquinone), it removes

125852.subject: Botany
125852.text: What represents the junction between the ovule and funicle?
125852.sol: The style is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma. The basal bulged part of the pistil is the ovary. Inside the ovary is the ovarian cavity (locule). The placenta is located inside the ovarian cavity. Recall the definition and types of placentation that you studied in Arising from the placenta are the megasporangia, commonly called ovules. The number of ovules in an ovary may be one (wheat, paddy, mango) to many (papaya, water melon, orchids). The Megasporangium (Ovule) : Let us familiarise ourselves with

125870.subject: Botany
125870.sol: Geitonogamy -Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. Although geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, genetically it is similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant. Xenogamy – Transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a different plant. This is the only type of pollination which during pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.

125983.subject: Botany
125983.text: Which process mimics sexual reproduction but does not involve fertilisation?
125983.sol: Although seeds, in general are the products of fertilisation, a few flowering plants such as some species of Asteraceae and grasses, have evolved a special mechanism, to produce seeds without fertilisation, called apomixis. What is fruit production without fertilisation called? Thus, apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction. There are several ways of development of apomictic seeds. In some species, the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into the embr

126913.subject: Botany
126913.text: Which of the following is not a derivative of cholesterol?
126913.sol: Among the given options, vitamin- B is not a derivative of cholesterol. It (cholesterol) is a type of lipid molecule. It is an essential structural component of all animal cell membranes. It also serves as a precursor for the biosynthesis of steroid hormones, bile salts and vitamin-D.

127108.subject: Botany
127108.text: The gases that produce green house effect are
options: CO ₂, ~N ₂ O , H ₂
127108.sol: Green house effect is the CO ₂ effect. It is due to CO ₂ layer in atmosphere and also by (CFCs) , SO ₂, NO ₂, CH ₄ . These gases come from factories, automobile, agriculture, refrigerators, deforestation. These gases entrap the solar heat and prevents the escape of heat from earth to outer space, thus increasing the temperature of earth which further lead to global warming.

127119.subject: Botany
options: The diversity at the species level.
The diversity of a single species at the genetic level over its distributional range.
The combined diversity of macromolecules within cells.
127119.sol: The diversity at the species level, for example, the Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghat

127236.subject: Botany
127236.text: What was the outcome of the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992?
options: All nations were called to take measures for conservation of biodiversity
All nations were called to sustainably utilize the benefits of biodiversity
190 countries pledged their commitment to achieve a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity
127236.sol: Biodiversity knows no political boundaries and its conservation is therefore a collective responsibility of all nations. The historic Convention on Biological Diversity (‘The Earth Summit’) held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992, called upon all nations to take appropriate measures for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilisation of its benefits . In a follow-up, the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in 2002 in Johannesburg, South Africa, 190 countries pledged their commitment to achieve by 2010, a s

127713.subject: Botany
127713.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers 2. Secondary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area 3. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 150 billion tons of organic matter. 4. Despite occupying about 70 percent of the surface, the produ
127713.sol: Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons of organic matter

127832.subject: Botany
127832.text: Most animals that live in deep oceanic waters are
127832.sol: Benthos is the community of organisms which live on, in, or near the sea bed, also known as the benthic zone. As no light is available in this zone of sea, the energy source for deep benthic ecosystem is often organic matter from higher water column which drifts down to the depths. This dead and decaying matter sustains the benthic organisms, and therefore, most organisms in benthic zone i.e., in deep oceanic waters, are scavengers or detritivores.

128354.subject: Zoology
128354.text: What type of cells in the Islets of Langerhans secrete insulin?
128354.sol: Pancreas is a composite gland (Figure 19.1) which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland. The endocrine pancreas consists of ‘Islets of Langerhans’. There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas representing only 1 to 2 per cent of the pancreatictissue. The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called α-cells and β-cells. The α-cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the β-cells secrete insulin. Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called di

128737.subject: Zoology
128737.text: Identify the correct set, which shows the name of the enzyme from where it is secreted and substrate upon which it acts.
128737.sol: Pepsin is released from peptic cells of the gastric gland on the stomach wall and it can digest milk protein caesin. Chymotrypsin is released from the intestine and digest proteins. Ptyalin is released from salivary glands and acts on starch.

128790.subject: Zoology
128790.text: What is the role of leucocytes in the blood?
128790.sol: Leucocytes are also known as white blood cells (WBC) as they are colorless due to the lack of haemoglobin. They are nucleated and are relatively lesser in number which averages 6000-8000 mm–3 of blood. Leucocytes are generally short lived. We have two main categories of WBCs – granulocytes and agranulocytes. Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the agranulocytes. Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 per cent) of the total WBCs and

128974.subject: Zoology
128974.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Haemoglobin molecules play a vital role in transport of respiratory gases Reason: A healthy individual has 11-15 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128974.sol: A healthy individual has 12-16 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood. These molecules play a significant role in transport of respiratory gases.

129045.subject: Zoology
129045.text: A newborn baby is diagnosed with severe anemia and jaundice. Medical investigation reveals that the baby's red blood cells are being destroyed by antibodies that crossed the placenta from the mother's blood. Which of the following parental blood group combinations and maternal history most likely resulted in this condition?
options: Mother is Rh ^ -ve , Father is Rh ^ +ve ; this is the mother's first pregnancy.
Mother is Rh ^ +ve , Father is Rh ^ -ve ; this is the mother's second pregnancy.
Mother is Rh ^ -ve , Father is Rh ^ -ve ; this is the mother's second pregnancy.
Mother is Rh ^ -ve , Father is Rh ^ +ve ; this is the mother's second pregnancy.
129045.sol: The condition described is erythroblastosis foetalis, which occurs due to Rh incompatibility between the mother and the foetus. For this condition to occur, the mother must be Rh ^ -ve and the foetus must be Rh ^ +ve . For the foetus to inherit the Rh antigen, the father must be Rh ^ +ve . During a first pregnancy with an Rh ^ +ve foetus, the Rh ^ -ve mother is typically not exposed to fetal blood until the time of delivery, so the first child is usually unaffected. Sensitization occurs at birth, leading to the pro

130109.subject: Zoology
130109.text: Match the structures in List-I with their corresponding features or functions in List-II. List-I List-II (A) Conducting part (I) Actual site of diffusion of O ₂ and CO ₂ between blood and atmospheric air (B) Exchange part (II) Divides at the level of 5th thoracic vertebra (C) Epiglottis (III) Brings inhaled air to body temperature (D) Trachea (IV) Prevents the entry of food into the larynx Choose the correct answer f
130109.sol: The conducting part of the respiratory system (external nostrils to terminal bronchioles) transports atmospheric air, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies it, and brings it to body temperature. Hence, (A) matches with (III). The exchange part (alveoli and their ducts) is the actual site of diffusion of O ₂ and CO ₂ between blood and atmospheric air. Hence, (B) matches with (I). The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that prevents the entry of food into the larynx during swallowing. Hence, (C) matches with (

130553.subject: Zoology
options: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Delhi
Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai
130553.sol: Research on various reproduction-related areas are encouraged and supported by governmental and non-governmental agencies to find out new methods and/or to improve upon the existing ones. ‘Saheli’–a new oral contraceptive for the females–was developed. by scientists at Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow, India. Better awareness about sex related matters, increased number of medically assisted deliveries and better post-natal care leading to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates, increased num

130762.subject: Zoology
130762.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding contraceptive methods. (A) Vaults (I) Natural method (B) Lippes loop (II) Barrier method (C) Progestasert (III) Non-medicated IUD (D) Coitus interruptus (IV) Hormone-releasing IUD Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
130762.sol: Vaults are barrier methods of contraception made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix. - Lippes loop is a non-medicated Intra Uterine Device (IUD). - Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUD. - Coitus interruptus is a natural method of contraception in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation. Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I). Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

131050.subject: Zoology
131050.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called Oogenesis. Reason: Oogenesis is the same process as of spermatogenesis.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131050.sol: The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called Oogenesis. Oogenesis is markedly different process from spermatogenesis.

131324.subject: Zoology
131324.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Monkey, apes and humans exhibit estrous cycle.
Urine is pale yellow and slightly alkaline.
Lots of enzymes are present in bile juice.
131324.sol: Great apes, humans goes through a menstrual cycle while monkey goes through estrous cycle. Urine is light yellow colored watery fluid which is slightly acidic. Bile juice does not contain any digestive enzymes.

131499.subject: Zoology
131499.text: What is the effect of a failure in cell division after DNA replication?
131499.sol: The DNA polymerases on their own cannot initiate the process of replication. Also the replication does not initiate randomly at any place in DNA. There is a definite region in E. coli DNA where the replication originates. Such regions are termed as origin of replication. It is because of the requirement of the origin of replication that a piece of DNA, if needed to be propagated during recombinant DNA procedures, requires a vector. The vectors provide the origin of replication. Further, not every detail of replicat

131787.subject: Zoology
131787.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) RNA polymerase (I) Joins Okazaki fragments (B) Helicase (II) Polymerizes deoxynucleotides (C) DNA ligase (III) Unwinds DNA double helix during replication (D) DNA polymerase (IV) Opens DNA helix during transcription Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
131787.sol: RNA polymerase catalyzes transcription and inherently facilitates the opening of the DNA helix during this process. Helicase is responsible for unwinding the DNA double helix specifically during DNA replication by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the two strands. DNA ligase joins the discontinuously synthesized DNA fragments (Okazaki fragments) during replication. DNA polymerase (DNA-dependent DNA polymerase) catalyzes the polymerization of deoxynucleotides to synthesize the new DNA strand. Therefore, the correc

132933.subject: Zoology
132933.text: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed a distinct stage in human evolution. Which of the following represents the characteristic features of the hominid that appeared chronologically immediately after this stage?
options: They had a brain capacity between 650-800 cc and probably did not eat meat.
They had a large brain around 900 cc and probably ate meat.
They arose in Africa, moved across continents and developed prehistoric cave art.
They had a brain size of 1400 cc and used hides to protect their body.
132933.sol: The fossils discovered in Java in 1891 belong to Homo erectus, who lived about 1.5 million years ago. According to the chronological sequence of human evolution, the hominid that appeared after Homo erectus is Neanderthal man (lived near east and central Asia between 1,00,000-40,000 years back). Neanderthal man had a brain size of 1400 cc, used hides to protect their body and buried their dead. Option 1 describes Homo habilis, which appeared before Homo erectus. Option 2 describes Homo erectus itself. Option 3 desc

133081.subject: Zoology
133081.sol: Some evolution occurs by random fluctuations in gene frequency called genetic drift. Such fluctuations are more likely to occur in a small population. Given frequency in small population changes by chance.

133735.subject: Zoology
133735.sol: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used for commercial production of ethanol. Microbes are also used for production of enzymes. Lipases are used in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily stains from the laundry. Bottled fruit juices bought from the market are clearer as compared to those made at home. This is because the bottled juices are clarified by the use of pectinases and proteases.

133952.subject: Zoology
133952.text: Read the following statements regarding bioactive molecules and their microbial sources. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Cyclosporin A acts as a blood-cholesterol lowering agent by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible fo
Statins are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus and act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsibl
Streptokinase is produced by a fungus and is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients.
Statins are blood-cholesterol lowering agents produced by a bacterium and act by competitively inhibiting chol
133952.sol: Statins are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus and are used as blood-cholesterol lowering agents. They act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol. Cyclosporin A is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum and is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients, not as a cholesterol-lowering agent. Streptokinase is produced by the bacterium Streptococcus (not a fungus) and is used as a 'clot buster', not as an immunosuppressive agent. Answer: Sta

133959.subject: Zoology
133959.text: Read the following statements carefully: (A) Statins are produced by a yeast, Monascus purpureus, and act as competitive inhibitors for the enzyme responsible for synthesis of cholesterol. (B) Cyclosporin A is produced by a bacterium, Trichoderma polysporum, and is used as an immunosuppressive agent. (C) Aspergillus niger is a fungus used for the commercial production of citric acid. (D) The 'clot buster' enzyme stre
133959.sol: Statement (A) is correct: Statins are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus and act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis. Statement (B) is incorrect: Cyclosporin A is produced by a fungus, Trichoderma polysporum, not a bacterium. Statement (C) is correct: Aspergillus niger is a fungus used for the commercial production of citric acid. Statement (D) is incorrect: Streptokinase is produced by the bacterium Streptococcus, not a fungus. Therefore, exactly two statements are co

134170.subject: Zoology
134170.text: What is the main reason for the growing realization of injustice, inadequate compensation and benefit sharing between developed and developing countries?
options: The exploitation of bio-resources and traditional knowledge without proper authorization.
The commercialization of bio-resources and traditional knowledge.
The development of modern applications using bio-resources and traditional knowledge.
The use of bio-resources and traditional knowledge to save time and effort.
134170.sol: Most of the industrialised nations are rich financially but poor in biodiversity and traditional knowledge. In contrast the developing and the underdeveloped world is rich in biodiversity and traditional knowledge related to bio-resources. Traditional knowledge related to bio-resources can be exploited to develop modern applications and can also be used to save time, effort and expenditure during their commercialisation. There has been growing realisation of the injustice, inadequate compensation and benefit sharin

134198.subject: Zoology
134198.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell/ explant is called totipotency. Reason: The nutrient medium must provide a carbon source such as sucrose and also inorganic salts, vitamins, amino acids and growth regulators like Auxins, Cytokinins, etc.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
134198.sol: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell/ explant is called totipotency. The nutrient medium must provide a carbon source such as sucrose and also inorganic salts, vitamins, amino acids and growth regulators like Auxins, Cytokinins, etc.

134402.subject: Zoology
options: The integration of natural science and organisms
134402.sol: It is used in a restricted sense today, to refer to such of those processes which use genetically modified organisms to achieve the same on a larger scale. Further, many other processes/techniques are also included under biotechnology. For example, in vitro fertilisation leading to a ‘test-tube’ baby, synthesising a gene and using it, developing a DNA vaccine or correcting a defective gene, are all part of biotechnology. The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) has given a definition of biotechnology that enc

135110.subject: Zoology
135110.text: What symbols are used to represent beneficial, detrimental, and neutral interspecific interactions?
options: - for beneficial, + for detrimental, 0 for neutral
+ for beneficial, - for detrimental, 0 for neutral

6a0e277b165ae1327797b407.subject: Biology
6a0e277b165ae1327797b407.text: The basic nature of histone proteins allows them to tightly pack the DNA helix. This property is due to the presence of positive charges on which specific part of their constituent basic amino acid residues?
6a0e277b165ae1327797b407.sol: Histone proteins are rich in basic amino acid residues, primarily lysine and arginine. These basic amino acids possess side chains (R groups) that carry a positive charge at physiological pH. The positive charges on the side chains of these amino acids interact strongly with the negatively charged phosphate groups of the DNA backbone, allowing histones to tightly pack the DNA helix into nucleosomes. Carboxyl groups are generally negatively charged, while peptide bonds and alpha-carbon atoms do not carry the positiv

6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fae.subject: Biology
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fae.text: Which of the following events of oogenesis occurs specifically during the embryonic development stage in human females?
options: Completion of meiosis I to form a large secondary oocyte
Formation of a couple of million oogonia within each fetal ovary
Transition of primary follicles into mature Graafian follicles
Extrusion of the second polar body
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fae.sol: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each fetal ovary. No more oogonia are formed and added after birth. Completion of meiosis I occurs just prior to ovulation during the reproductive years. Transition of primary follicles into mature Graafian follicles occurs during the menstrual cycle after puberty. Extrusion of the second polar body occurs only after the entry of the sperm into the secondary oocyte (fertilization).

6a2109b2219e1ae5a17229a3.subject: Biology

options: It is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes.
It is impermeable to water but allows active transport of electrolytes.
It actively secretes urea and potassium ions into the tubular lumen.
It allows conditional reabsorption of water under the influence of ADH.
6a2109b2219e1ae5a17229a3.sol: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. As the glomerular filtrate moves down this segment, water moves out of the tubule into the hyperosmotic medullary interstitium due to osmosis. This loss of water concentrates the filtrate, increasing its osmolarity from about 300 mOsmol/L in the cortex to about 1200 mOsmol/L in the inner medulla. Presence of a single ovule in each ovary
Flowers are large, brightly coloured, and rich in nectar

6a13e468688ac6d0667aad63.sol: Wind-pollinated flowers (anemophilous flowers) typically possess certain characteristic features to facilitate pollination by air currents. Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
6a16f3287cfacf7984f8672c.sol: In the lac operon, the i gene codes for the repressor protein. The term ' i ' does not refer to inducer, rather it is derived from the word inhibitor. 95210.subject: Botany
95210.text: Lenticels are formed by rupturing of the epidermis by
95210.sol: In certain regions, the phellogen cuts off closely arranged parenchymatous cells on the outer side instead of cork cells. These parenchymatous cells soon rupture the epidermis, forming lens-shaped openings called lenticels. Lenticels permit the exchange of gases between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissue of the stem. These occur in most woody trees.

95304.sol: It is long,narrow cells with thick and lignified cell wall having a pits. They are usually dead and without protoplasts. They provides mechanical support to organ.

95359.text: Which one of the following is a matching set of the class and some of its main distinguishing features, classification, and examples?

95359.sol: Reptiles are classified under division Gnathostomata and superclass Tetrapoda. The class name Reptilia refers to their creeping or crawling mode of locomotion (Latin, repere or reptum, to creep or crawl). They are mostly terrestrial animals and their body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales, or scutes. They do not have external ear openings. Tympanum represents ear. 95626.subject: Botany
95626.text: Choose the correct statement regarding retrovirus.
options: An RNA virus that can synthesize DNA during infection.
A DNA virus that can synthesize RNA during infection.
95626.sol: Retrovirus, any of a group of viruses that belong to the family retroviridae and that characteristically carry their genetic blueprint in the form of ribonucleic acid (RNA). They have ssRNA as genetic material. It is a type of RNA virus that inserts a copy of its genome into the DNA of a host cell that it invades, thus changing the genome of that cell. It uses a special enzyme called reverse transcriptase to translate its genetic information into DNA. That DNA can then integrate into the host cell's DNA. Once integ

95843.subject: Botany
95843.text: How many organisms in the list given below are autotrophs? ( Lactobacillus, Nostoc, Chara, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, Streptomyces, Saccharomyces, Trypanosoma, Porphyra, Laminaria )
95843.sol: Autotrophic organisms are those organisms that are capable of synthesizing food themselves from inorganic and organic substances. Autotrophs can be of two types: photoautotrophs and chemoautotrophs. In photoautotrophic organisms, there is chlorophyll present due to which they can prepare their food through carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight whereas chemoautotrophs obtain energy through food by chemical source instead of light. Out of the given examples, photoautotrophs are Nostoc, Chara, Porphyra,

96360.subject: Botany
96360.text: A teacher was trying to show the different stages of a type of cell division to the students. At a particular stage, it was observed that the chromosomes were separating but there was no splitting of centromeres. This stage would be
96360.sol: Meiosis is a reductional division process where the cell undergoes two successive division processes to reduce chromosome number to half. It is divided into the meiotic stages I and II. Anaphase I is part of the meiotic stage I, where the sister chromatids separate from its homologous counterpart. The chromatids centromere remains intact in this stage and do not separate. Their separation occurs in anaphase II in meiotic stage II.

96486.subject: Botany
96486.text: Read the following statements. With respect to the ecological pyramid, mark the correct statements. a. In most of the ecosystems, pyramids of number, energy and biomass are upright. b. Producers are generally more in number or biomass than herbivores in an upright pyramid. c. Herbivores are less in number and biomass than carnivores in an inverted pyramid. d. Energy content is higher at a lower trophic level than tha
options: a, b, and c are correct
a, b and d are correct
96486.sol: All the statements explain the characteristics of pyramids. In most ecosystems, all the pyramids of number, energy or biomass are upright, i.e., producers are more in number and biomass than the herbivores, and herbivores are more in number and biomass than the carnivores. Also, energy at a lower trophic level is always more than that at a higher level.

97554.subject: Botany
97554.text: Brown algae vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment:
97554.sol: The members of Phaeophyceae or brown algae possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

6a7a1ff8cf49fac6cdd68573.text: A water sprinkler placed on the ground sprays water in all directions with a constant speed. The maximum circular area covered by the water on the ground is 144 m ^2 . 6a7a1ff8f3fc6ae287dd2162.text: An ideal monoatomic gas is enclosed in a rigid, perfectly spherical vessel at a pressure of 3 10^5 ~Pa . If the total internal energy of the gas is 4.8 10^6 ~J , the radius of the spherical vessel is _______ m .

6a7a1ff89da84d4a66e2a238.text: Consider the following statements regarding some common molecules: (A) The bond angle in OF ₂ is less than the bond angle in H ₂ O . (B) The dipole moment of NF ₃ is greater than the dipole moment of NH ₃ . (C) The oxidation state of oxygen in OF ₂ is +2 . (D) The dipole moment of H ₂ O is greater than the dipole moment of OF ₂ . Which of the given statements are correct?
6a7a1ff89da84d4a66e2a238.sol: Statement (A): In OF ₂ , fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen, so the bonding electron pairs are pulled away from the central oxygen atom. This decreases the bond pair-bond pair repulsion compared to H ₂ O , allowing the lone pairs to compress the F - O - F angle to approximately 103^ , which is less than the H - O - H angle ( 104.5^ ). Statement (A) is correct. Statement (B): In NH ₃ , the orbital dipole due to the lone pair is in the same direction as the resultant dipole moment of the three N - H bonds.

6a7a1ff838466994a4616ae6.text: The limiting molar ionic conductivities of H^+ and A^- ions are 350 ~S~cm ^2 ~mol ⁻¹ and 50 ~S~cm ^2 ~mol ⁻¹ respectively.
